text:
Elaine: Quick design review — the pipeline editor form is throwing a lot of micro-errors. Thinking: keep field-level inline errors for typed mistakes, but show destructive action confirmations (delete dataset, reset infra) as a focused modal with typed-confirm + clear consequences. Thoughts? :thinking: Sam: I like inline for validation that blocks submission. For destructive actions we should surface the exact item name in the modal and require typed-confirm (e.g., type ‘delete my-dataset’). That prevents accidental clicks. Alex: Agree re: typed-confirm for deletes, but accessibility note: typed-confirm modal needs aria-live and clear focus management. If someone uses voiceover, the required instruction should be announced. Courtney: Can we avoid duplicating error messages? Right now inline + top summary duplicate the same text. My suggestion: inline for the field + summary for submit-time aggregate with anchors to first invalid field. Summary should only appear on submit. morgan: +1 to Courtney. Also, required markers: a lot of confusion about the asterisk meaning. Proposal: explicit copy ("Required") in helper text for a11y and hide asterisk from screen readers. Elaine: Good call. Example ARIA pattern I was thinking of: ```html
Name is required.
``` We'd pair that with CSS to visually show asterisk but keep screen readers relying on aria-required and helper text. Alex: That works. For the summary anchor links we should set focus to the first invalid field when clicking the link. Also ensure the summary itself has role="status" so screen readers know something changed. Sam: Small copy nit for the destructive modal: current copy is boring: "Are you sure you want to delete?" How about: "Delete dataset \"analytics-prod\" — This action cannot be undone. Type the dataset name to confirm." Button labels: Primary = "Delete dataset", Secondary = "Cancel", Danger style on primary. Courtney: Also consider offering an undo toast for soft-deletes (if backend supports). Modal + typed-confirm for permanent deletes, toast+undo for user-facing soft-delete flows. morgan: One more accessibility nit: color-only danger cues. Add an icon + textual hint (e.g., "This will permanently remove all runs and logs."). Screen reader should get that as part of modal content. Elaine: Great — action items: 1) Update modal copy and add typed-confirm pattern examples (Sam), 2) Add aria snippets and guidance on asterisk usage (Alex/morgan), 3) Change summary to appear only on submit with anchor links and focus management (Courtney), 4) Product to decide soft-delete vs hard-delete UX paths (me). I'll throw a quick mock into Figma tonight. @Alex can you review the aria snippets after I push? :thumbsup: Alex: Yep, will review after your mock. If you can paste the Figma link here I’ll check the focus order. aria-bot: Accessibility checklist reminder: ensure focus trap in modal, role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and visible focus indicator for keyboard users. Elaine: thanks all — closing this thread once I upload the mock. :)
